state.spec: Add SVG rendering + an SVG-as-editable-document layer to flow, satisfying the contract tests test_svg.py and test_svg_doc.py exactly. (1) Add a pure function to_svg(wf: WorkflowDef) -> str to the EXISTING module packages/flow/src/flow/graph.py (keep to_ascii/to_mermaid and all existing code intact). It renders the workflow as a valid standalone SVG: one <rect>+<text> per node (id + [type], entry marked), one arrow per edge, conditional edges labelled via the existing _condition_label helper, loop edges labelled 'loop xN'. Deterministic geometry. CRITICAL FOR XML VALIDITY: EVERY piece of text placed inside an SVG <text> element or attribute — node ids, type labels, AND edge labels from _condition_label (which can contain '<', '>', '&', '{{...}}', quotes, arbitrary prose) — MUST be XML-escaped with xml.sax.saxutils.escape before being put in the string. The output must always parse via xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring even when node ids or condition text contain special characters. (2) Create NEW module packages/flow/src/flow/builder/svg_doc.py: workflow_to_svg_document(wf) -> str calls to_svg, then embeds the workflow_to_dict(wf) JSON inside a child metadata element with id 'flow-workflow' under the <svg> root. Do NOT use a CDATA section (the JSON payload can itself contain ']]>' — a workflow may describe SVG/CDATA in its prompts — which breaks CDATA and makes the SVG non-well-formed). Instead build the metadata element with xml.etree.ElementTree: create an Element, set its .text to json.dumps(workflow_to_dict(wf)) (ElementTree auto-escapes on serialize), and ET.tostring it; OR json.dumps then xml.sax.saxutils.escape and insert as element text. read_workflow_from_svg(source: str | pathlib.Path) -> WorkflowDef parses the whole SVG via ET.fromstring, finds the element whose id attribute == 'flow-workflow', reads element .text (ElementTree auto-UNescapes), json.loads it, parse_workflow it; raise flow.errors.WorkflowValidationError if the marker is missing. dump_workflow_svg(wf, path) writes the document. NOTE: the contract runs the round-trip over ALL examples/*.json including svg_codegen.json itself, whose prompts contain XML/CDATA/special characters — your escaping must handle that self-referential case. The embedded JSON is the source of truth; the drawing is derived.
